Resources

Glossary and Data

Use these definitions for reference. The required lessons introduce terms where you first need them.

acrosome

A specialized cap on the sperm head involved in interaction with the oocyte's coverings.

Review: Division and differentiation
acrosome reaction

Release of enzymes and membrane changes that help a sperm cell cross layers surrounding an oocyte.

Review: Gametes meet
allantois

An extra-embryonic structure that contributes to parts of the umbilical cord and urinary-bladder developmental pathway.

Review: Support membranes
amnion

The extra-embryonic membrane that encloses the fluid-filled amniotic cavity.

Review: Support membranes
amniotic fluid

Fluid surrounding the developing embryo or fetus that cushions, permits movement, and supports a stable local environment.

anabolic steroid

A steroid substance with actions related to testosterone; an outside androgen signal can alter feedback and suppress normal sperm production.

Review: Feedback and evidence
androgen

A class of steroid hormones, including testosterone and dihydrotestosterone, that act through androgen receptors.

andropause

A term sometimes used for age-associated testicular hormone changes; it does not mean an abrupt universal cessation of sperm production.

Review: Feedback and evidence
anterior pituitary

The hormone-producing front part of the pituitary gland below the brain.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
artificial insemination

Placement of sperm in the reproductive tract to assist fertilization within the body.

Review: Implantation and reproductive technology
association

A measured relationship between variables that does not, by itself, establish that one variable caused the other.

asymptomatic

Present without noticeable symptoms; an asymptomatic infection may still be transmissible or biologically important.

axis

A labelled reference line on a graph indicating a variable and its measurement scale.

Review: Two coordinated cycles
barrier method

A reproductive-health method that physically reduces movement or contact, with effectiveness depending on the specific method and use.

Review: Hormonal technologies and perspectives
benefit

A favourable outcome for a specified person, group or system, evaluated using stated criteria.

Review: Hormonal technologies and perspectives
blastocyst

An early developmental stage with an outer trophoblast, inner cell mass, and fluid-filled cavity.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
blastomere

One of the smaller cells produced by early cleavage divisions.

bulbourethral gland

One of the small glands below the prostate that release fluid into the urethra; also called a Cowper gland.

capacitation

Functional changes sperm undergo in the female reproductive tract that help prepare them for fertilization.

Review: Gametes meet
causal inference

A reasoned judgment about whether and how one factor contributes to an outcome, based on design, mechanism, alternatives, and converging evidence.

causal limit

A reason the available evidence cannot establish that one factor caused another.

Review: Developmental evidence
cell migration

Movement of cells from one location to another during development or other biological processes.

Review: Gastrulation establishes layers
cervical dilation

Opening of the cervix during labour.

Review: Birth and the transition
cervical stretch

Distension of the cervix that can contribute to the positive-feedback signalling of labour.

Review: Labour and positive feedback
cervix

The lower, narrow region of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
chorion

An outer extra-embryonic membrane that contributes to the fetal portion of the placenta and chorionic villi.

Review: Support membranes
chorionic villus

A branching placental structure containing fetal vessels and providing a large exchange surface near maternal blood.

ciliary transport

Movement of material along a surface by coordinated beating of tiny cell extensions called cilia.

Review: Structure and reproductive function
cleavage

Rapid early mitotic divisions that increase cell number without a proportional increase in overall conceptus size.

Review: Cleavage and blastocyst formation
comparison

Examination of similarities and differences between specified conditions or observations.

Review: Feedback and evidence
competing explanation

An alternative mechanism that could account for some or all of the same observations and must be tested against evidence.

conception control

Methods intended to reduce the probability of pregnancy by acting at defined reproductive steps.

confounder

Another factor related to both the proposed cause and the measured outcome, which can distort the apparent relationship between them.

Review: Environmental influence and evidence
confounding

Distortion that occurs when another factor is related to both the proposed cause and the measured outcome.

continuity

Reliable transmission of biological information and life processes across cells or generations.

contraception

Methods intended to reduce the probability of pregnancy by acting at defined reproductive steps.

Review: Hormonal technologies and perspectives
controlled variable

A factor intentionally kept consistent so it does not confound the tested comparison.

Review: Feedback and evidence
convergence

Agreement among independent evidence types that strengthens an explanation.

corpus luteum

Temporary hormone-producing tissue formed from a follicle after ovulation; it releases progesterone and estrogen.

Review: Ovaries and supporting tissues
Cowper glands

Small glands below the prostate that release fluid into the urethra; also called bulbourethral glands.

Review: Semen and accessory glands
cryopreservation

Storage of cells or tissues at very low temperature to slow biological activity for later use.

cycle variation

Differences in the timing or length of reproductive cycles; an illustrative 28-day model is not universal.

Review: Graphs and cycle variation
data

Recorded observations or measurements with their context, units and method.

Review: Feedback and evidence
delivery

The birth stage in which the fetus passes out of the uterus.

Review: Labour and positive feedback
differentiation

The regulated process through which cells develop specialized gene-expression patterns, structures, and functions.

Review: Division and differentiation
diffusion

Net movement of particles down a concentration gradient through random molecular motion.

Review: Maternal and fetal circulation
digestive lining

The layer of cells facing the internal space of the digestive tract.

Review: Layer-to-tissue relationships
dihydrotestosterone

A potent androgen produced from testosterone in selected tissues and involved in parts of reproductive development.

diploid

Having two chromosome sets, conventionally written 2n.

Review: Gametes and chromosome sets
discriminating evidence

A result expected to differ between competing explanations and therefore help distinguish them.

dose

The amount of an agent delivered or received, with its units and exposure conditions stated.

Review: Organ formation across development
dose-response

A pattern in which the magnitude or probability of an effect changes with exposure amount.

ductus deferens

A muscular duct that transports sperm from the epididymis toward the ejaculatory duct; also called the vas deferens.

ectoderm

The primary germ layer that contributes to the epidermis, nervous system, and selected sensory structures.

Review: Gastrulation establishes layers
ejaculatory duct

A short duct that carries sperm and seminal-vesicle fluid into the urethra.

Review: The transport pathway
embryo

A developing organism in an early stage of organ formation; human stage labels must specify the dating convention.

Review: Reproductive development and health
embryo transfer

Placement of an embryo into a uterus during an assisted-reproduction procedure.

Review: Implantation and reproductive technology
embryonic period

The prenatal period emphasizing implantation, gastrulation, body-plan establishment, and early organogenesis.

endocrine tissue

Hormone-secreting tissue; different endocrine organs can have different embryonic origins.

Review: Layer-to-tissue relationships
endoderm

The primary germ layer that contributes to much of the digestive and respiratory epithelial lining and to selected glands.

Review: Gastrulation establishes layers
endometrium

The hormone-responsive inner lining of the uterus where implantation may occur.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
epidermis

The outer surface layer of skin, distinct from the deeper supporting tissue.

Review: Layer-to-tissue relationships
epididymis

A coiled duct where sperm mature and are stored after leaving the testes.

Review: The transport pathway
estrogen

A class of steroid hormones involved in reproductive-tissue function, secondary sex characteristics, cycle regulation, and feedback.

Review: Ovaries and supporting tissues
evidence ledger

A structured record separating observations, sources, units, timing, interpretations, and limits.

Fallopian tube

A uterine tube that receives an ovulated oocyte and is the usual site of fertilization; its lining and muscular wall support transport toward the uterus.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
feedback

Return information from a response or downstream signal that changes later activity in a control system.

feedback suppression

Reduction of an upstream signal when a downstream response feeds back on its source.

Review: Feedback and evidence
fertility

The biological capacity or probability of reproduction, influenced by many interacting factors and not established by one classroom measure.

Review: The transport pathway
fertility probability

The chance of a specified reproductive outcome under stated conditions; it depends on many factors and is not established by one classroom measurement.

Review: Structure and reproductive function
fertilization

A sequence in which sperm and oocyte membranes and genetic material combine to begin development of a zygote.

Review: Gametes and chromosome sets
fetal period

The prenatal period emphasizing growth, maturation, and increasing functional integration after the embryonic period.

fetus

The developing human from the ninth week after fertilization until birth, when growth and organ maturation predominate.

Review: Support membranes
fimbriae

Finger-like extensions near the opening of a uterine tube that help receive an ovulated oocyte.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
flagellum

A long cellular extension that produces movement, as in the tail of a sperm cell.

Review: Division and differentiation
follicle

An ovarian structure containing an oocyte and surrounding support and hormone-producing cells.

Review: Ovaries and supporting tissues
follicular phase

The ovarian-cycle phase during which follicles develop before ovulation.

Review: Two coordinated cycles
FSH

Follicle-stimulating hormone: a signal from the anterior pituitary that supports growth of the cells around a developing egg and acts through Sertoli cells to support sperm development.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
gamete

A haploid reproductive cell—sperm or egg lineage cell—that can contribute one chromosome set at fertilization.

gastrulation

Early embryonic cell movements that establish primary germ layers and body organization.

Review: Gastrulation establishes layers
gender

A social and personal dimension of identity and roles that cannot be inferred from one chromosome, hormone, or anatomical measure.

germ layer

One of the primary embryonic tissue layers—ectoderm, mesoderm, or endoderm—from which tissues develop.

Review: Gastrulation establishes layers
GnRH

Gonadotropin-releasing hormone: a chemical signal from the brain region called the hypothalamus that stimulates release of FSH and LH from the front part of the pituitary gland.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
gonad

An ovary or testis; an organ that produces gametes and reproductive hormones.

gonadotropin

A hormone such as FSH or LH that acts on gonadal targets.

growth hormone

A protein hormone released by the anterior pituitary that contributes to growth and metabolism; also called hGH or somatotropin.

Review: Feedback and evidence
haploid

Having one chromosome set, conventionally written n.

Review: Gametes and chromosome sets
hCG

Human chorionic gonadotropin; a trophoblast-derived hormone that helps maintain corpus-luteum function early in pregnancy.

Review: Corpus luteum and the endometrium
hormonal contraception

A conception-control approach that uses hormones to change ovulation, mucus, endometrial, or related reproductive conditions depending on the method.

hormonal method

A conception-control approach that uses hormones to change ovulation, mucus, endometrial, or related reproductive conditions depending on the method.

Review: Technologies, infertility and perspectives
HPV

Human papillomavirus; a group of viruses, some of which can cause warts and some of which can contribute to cancers after persistent infection.

hypothalamus

A brain region that integrates information and releases signals to help regulate the pituitary gland.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
implantation

Attachment and embedding of a hatched blastocyst in a receptive uterine endometrium.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
in vitro fertilization

An assisted-reproduction process in which oocytes and sperm are combined or injected in a laboratory before an embryo may be transferred.

infertility reversal

An attempt to restore a disrupted reproductive pathway; restoring one function does not guarantee conception.

Review: Technologies, infertility and perspectives
inflammation

A coordinated tissue response to injury or infection that can protect but may also contribute to pain, swelling, or tissue damage.

informed consent

A voluntary decision made with understandable information about purpose, benefits, risks, alternatives, and the right to refuse.

inhibin

A gonadal hormone that provides feedback reducing FSH release.

Review: Feedback and evidence
inner cell mass

The blastocyst cell cluster that contributes to the embryo proper and some extra-embryonic tissues.

Review: Cleavage and blastocyst formation
interstitial cell

A cell between the sperm-producing tubules of a testis that releases testosterone; in this context, also called a Leydig cell.

interstitial cells

Cells between the sperm-producing tubes of a testis that release the hormone testosterone into blood; also called Leydig cells.

Review: Compartments of the testes
intrauterine device

A small device placed in the uterus that reduces pregnancy probability through method-specific local mechanisms.

IVF

An assisted-reproduction process in which oocytes and sperm are combined or injected in a laboratory before an embryo may be transferred.

Review: Implantation and reproductive technology
lactation

Production and delivery of milk by mammary glands after birth, regulated by endocrine and neural signals.

LH

Luteinizing hormone: a signal from the anterior pituitary that stimulates testosterone release in testes and helps trigger egg release and formation of temporary hormone-producing tissue in ovaries.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
LH surge

A brief marked increase in luteinizing hormone associated with final follicular changes and ovulation.

Review: Follicle growth and changing feedback
limitation

A boundary on what a method, dataset or model can establish.

Review: Follicle growth and changing feedback
luteal phase

The ovarian-cycle phase after ovulation when the corpus luteum produces progesterone and estrogen.

Review: Two coordinated cycles
meiotic completion

Finishing a meiotic division; in a typical human secondary oocyte, meiosis II completes after sperm-triggered activation.

Review: Oogenesis and meiotic pauses
menopause

The end of recurring menstrual cycles associated with loss of ovarian follicular function; the preceding transition can involve changing cycles and hormones.

Review: Graphs and cycle variation
menstrual cycle

A coordinated set of ovarian, uterine, and hormonal changes conventionally tracked from the first day of menstrual bleeding.

menstruation

Shedding of much of the functional endometrial layer after ovarian-hormone support declines in a non-pregnant cycle.

Review: Two coordinated cycles
mesoderm

The primary germ layer that contributes to muscle, skeleton, connective tissues, blood, kidneys, gonads, and many reproductive structures.

Review: Gastrulation establishes layers
milk ejection

Movement of milk into mammary ducts when surrounding contractile cells respond to oxytocin; it differs from making milk.

Review: Milk synthesis and release
milk synthesis

Production of milk by mammary secretory cells, supported by prolactin; it differs from milk ejection.

Review: Milk synthesis and release
model

A simplified representation used to explain observations or make testable predictions under stated assumptions.

Review: Compartments of the testes
morphogenesis

Development of tissue and organ shape through coordinated growth, movement, folding, adhesion, and cell death.

morula

A compact ball of cells formed by early divisions after fertilization, before a fluid-filled blastocyst develops.

Review: Cleavage and blastocyst formation
muscle

Tissue specialized for contraction and force production.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
myoepithelial cell

A contractile cell around mammary secretory structures that responds to oxytocin during milk ejection.

negative feedback

Control in which a response reduces the original deviation or lowers upstream stimulation.

Review: Feedback and evidence
nervous tissue

Specialized cells and supporting tissue that receive, process or transmit information.

Review: Layer-to-tissue relationships
neural crest

Migratory cells arising near the neural tube that contribute to diverse structures, including parts of the peripheral nervous system.

neural plate

A thickened region of embryonic ectoderm that folds during early nervous-system development.

Review: Organ formation across development
neural tube

An embryonic structure formed through neural-plate folding that gives rise to the brain and spinal cord.

Review: Layer-to-tissue relationships
neurulation

The developmental process in which the neural plate folds and forms the neural tube, a foundation of the central nervous system.

Review: Organ formation across development
newborn transition

Changes that allow a newborn to exchange gases and obtain support outside the placenta.

Review: Birth and the transition
observation

Information recorded using a specified method; an explanation of its cause is an inference.

Review: Compartments of the testes
obstruction

A blockage that reduces movement through a passage; it does not necessarily stop production upstream.

Review: The transport pathway
oocyte

A developing female germ cell; stage names such as primary and secondary oocyte reflect meiotic state.

Review: Division and differentiation
oocyte retrieval

A medical procedure used to collect oocytes from ovarian follicles for assisted reproduction.

organogenesis

Developmental formation and organization of organs from interacting tissues.

Review: Organ formation across development
ovarian cycle

The sequence of follicular development, ovulation, and luteal activity in the ovaries.

Review: Two coordinated cycles
ovary

A reproductive organ that contains developing egg cells and releases reproductive hormones.

Review: Ovaries and supporting tissues
ovulation

Release of a secondary oocyte and surrounding cells from a mature ovarian follicle.

Review: Ovaries and supporting tissues
oxytocin

A hormone made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary; it contributes to uterine contraction and milk ejection.

Review: Labour and positive feedback
parturition

The coordinated process of labour and birth.

Review: Labour and positive feedback
pathogen

A biological agent, such as a bacterium or virus, capable of causing infection or disease.

peak

The highest observed value in a defined region or interval; sparse observations may miss the actual maximum.

Review: Follicle growth and changing feedback
pelvic inflammatory disease

Inflammation and infection of upper reproductive-tract tissues that can follow some untreated infections and may affect fertility.

penis

An external organ containing a urethral passage that can deliver semen.

Review: The transport pathway
placenta

A temporary exchange, endocrine, immune, and metabolic organ formed from fetal and maternal tissues during pregnancy.

Review: Cleavage and blastocyst formation
placental barrier

The tissue interface separating maternal and fetal circulations while permitting selective exchange.

placental delivery

Expulsion of the placenta and associated membranes after the fetus is delivered.

Review: Birth and the transition
placental exchange

Transfer of substances across the placental interface between normally separate maternal and fetal circulations.

Review: Support membranes
polar body

A small haploid cell produced by unequal cytokinesis during oogenesis that usually does not become an egg.

Review: Oogenesis and meiotic pauses
polyspermy block

Changes following fertilization that reduce entry of additional sperm into the oocyte.

Review: Combining chromosome sets
positive feedback

Control in which a response amplifies the initiating change until an endpoint interrupts the loop.

Review: Follicle growth and changing feedback
primary oocyte

A developing oocyte that has entered meiosis I and may remain arrested in prophase I for years.

Review: Oogenesis and meiotic pauses
primary sex characteristic

A structure directly involved in reproduction, such as an ovary or testis.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
primary spermatocyte

A diploid germ cell that has replicated its DNA and enters meiosis I during spermatogenesis.

Review: Gametes and chromosome sets
progesterone

A steroid hormone that supports secretory endometrial conditions, pregnancy-related changes, and reproductive feedback.

Review: Ovaries and supporting tissues
prolactin

An anterior-pituitary hormone that supports milk production in mammary tissue.

Review: Milk synthesis and release
proliferative phase

The uterine-cycle phase in which estrogen supports rebuilding and growth of the endometrium.

pronucleus

A haploid parental nucleus present during early fertilization before the parental chromosome sets participate in the first mitosis.

Review: Combining chromosome sets
prostaglandin

A locally acting lipid signal involved in processes including cervical change and uterine contraction.

Review: Labour and positive feedback
prostate gland

A male accessory gland that contributes fluid to semen.

Review: Semen and accessory glands
receptive endometrium

A uterine lining in a physiological state that can support blastocyst attachment and implantation.

Review: Implantation and reproductive technology
receptor

A protein that binds a signal and initiates or changes a cellular response.

relative concentration

A concentration expressed against a reference scale rather than necessarily in absolute chemical units.

Review: Follicle growth and changing feedback
reproduction

Biological processes that produce new organisms and transmit genetic information across generations.

reproductive structures

Organs and tissues involved in forming gametes, transporting them or supporting reproductive processes.

Review: The transport pathway
respiratory lining

The layer of cells facing the air passages of the respiratory system.

Review: Layer-to-tissue relationships
responsive target

A cell or tissue with the receptors and internal machinery needed to respond to a particular signal.

Review: Reproductive development and health
revision

A reasoned change to a prediction, explanation or plan after considering evidence or feedback.

Review: Structure and reproductive function
revision rule

A stated result or condition that would cause an explanation or decision to be changed.

route

The path by which a substance enters or moves through a system.

Review: The transport pathway
secondary oocyte

The cell produced after meiosis I in oogenesis; in humans it is typically arrested in metaphase II until fertilization.

Review: Ovaries and supporting tissues
secondary sex characteristic

A pubertal trait influenced by hormones that is not itself a gamete-producing or gamete-transporting organ.

Review: Hormone sources and targets
secondary spermatocyte

A haploid cell produced by meiosis I that proceeds through meiosis II during spermatogenesis.

Review: Division and differentiation
secretory phase

The progesterone-supported uterine phase in which the endometrium becomes more glandular and secretory after ovulation.

semen

Fluid containing sperm when present plus secretions from reproductive accessory glands.

Review: The transport pathway
seminal vesicle

One of a pair of glands that add a substantial part of the fluid in semen; it does not produce sperm.

seminal vesicles

Paired glands that add a substantial part of the fluid in semen; they do not produce sperm.

Review: The transport pathway
seminiferous tubule

A coiled tube inside a testis where sperm cells develop among supporting cells.

seminiferous tubules

Coiled tubes inside the testes where sperm cells develop among supporting cells.

Review: Compartments of the testes
Sertoli cell

A supporting cell within a sperm-producing tubule of a testis; it nourishes developing sperm and helps regulate their local conditions.

Sertoli cells

Supporting cells within the sperm-producing tubes of a testis; they nourish developing sperm and regulate their local conditions.

Review: Compartments of the testes
sex characteristic

A chromosomal, gonadal, hormonal, anatomical, or secondary physical trait related to sexual development; no one measure represents every dimension.

sexually transmitted infection

An infection that can be transmitted through sexual contact; pathogens, symptoms, prevention, testing, and treatment differ.

skeleton

The supporting framework of bones and cartilage in the body.

Review: Layer-to-tissue relationships
spermatid

A haploid cell produced by meiosis II that differentiates into a sperm cell.

Review: Division and differentiation
spermatogonium

A precursor cell in the sperm-producing lineage with two chromosome sets; its divisions can maintain precursor cells and produce cells that develop toward sperm.

Review: Gametes and chromosome sets
spermatozoon

A specialized sperm cell carrying one chromosome set and able, under suitable conditions, to interact with a developing egg cell.

Review: Semen and accessory glands
SRY

A gene region commonly located on the Y chromosome that can initiate a testis-development pathway; gene location and response can vary.

sterilization

A procedure intended as highly effective permanent conception control by interrupting gamete transport or reproductive anatomy.

Review: Technologies, infertility and perspectives
STI

An infection that can be transmitted through sexual contact; pathogens, symptoms, prevention, testing, and treatment differ.

Review: Reproductive development and health
suckling

Stimulation associated with an infant feeding that can activate prolactin and oxytocin pathways.

Review: Milk synthesis and release
temporal plausibility

The requirement that a proposed cause occur early enough and in the right developmental sequence to influence an outcome.

teratogen

An environmental agent that can disrupt development under particular dose, route, timing, and biological conditions.

Review: Environmental influence and evidence
testes

Paired reproductive organs that support sperm development and release hormones, including testosterone.

Review: Compartments of the testes
testosterone

A chemical messenger made mainly by cells between the sperm-producing tubes of the testes; it contributes to reproductive development, function and feedback.

Review: Compartments of the testes
timing

The position and order of events relative to a clearly stated starting point or interval.

Review: Reproductive development and health
trimester

One of three broad time divisions used to describe pregnancy; biological processes overlap these boundaries.

Review: Organ formation across development
trophoblast

The blastocyst outer cell layer that contributes to implantation and the fetal portion of the placenta.

Review: Cleavage and blastocyst formation
umbilical artery

A fetal vessel carrying blood from the fetus toward the placenta.

Review: Maternal and fetal circulation
umbilical cord

The connection carrying fetal blood vessels between the developing fetus and the placenta.

Review: Support membranes
umbilical vein

A fetal vessel carrying oxygen- and nutrient-enriched blood from the placenta toward the fetus.

Review: Maternal and fetal circulation
uncertainty

A transparent description of limits in measurement, sampling, models, evidence, or prediction.

urethra

A duct carrying urine and, at different times in typical male anatomy, semen to the exterior.

Review: The transport pathway
uterine cycle

The recurring changes in the endometrium, including shedding, rebuilding and secretory preparation.

Review: Two coordinated cycles
uterine tube

A duct, also called a Fallopian tube, that receives an ovulated oocyte and is the usual site of fertilization.

uterus

A muscular reproductive organ containing the endometrium and supporting implantation and prenatal development.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
vaccination

Use of a vaccine to develop an immune response to a selected pathogen or its harmful products. A vaccine can supply antigens or instructions that allow cells to make an antigen.

vagina

A muscular canal connecting the cervix with the exterior.

Review: Transport and implantation surfaces
variables

Features that can change, be controlled or be measured in an investigation.

Review: Feedback and evidence
variation

Differences among organisms arising from genetic recombination, mutation, development, and environmental context.

vas deferens

A muscular duct that transports sperm from the epididymis toward the ejaculatory duct; also called the ductus deferens.

Review: The transport pathway
Y chromosome

A sex chromosome that typically carries a testis-development signal in humans; its presence alone does not establish every sex trait.

Review: Reproductive development and health
zona pellucida

The protective protein-and-sugar layer around a developing egg cell and the early developing cell group before it hatches from this layer.

Review: Gametes meet
zygote

The diploid cell formed after fertilization and combination of parental chromosome sets.

Review: Gametes and chromosome sets
